svg.title: a freshly generated project passes its own quality gate: the toolbox ships dependencies that pass its own OSV scan
svg.text: a freshly generated project passes its own quality gate
Scenario: the toolbox ships dependencies that pass its own OSV scan

g.text: Then the toolbox's own OSV scan reads the lockfile or requirements file of every tool that
has one and finds no known vulnerability
GitLab's page for the toolbox's own code:megalinter job, with OSV as its only scanner, checked against the live
vulnerability database. The scanner's command leaves no .config folder out.
The Scanned lines name seven files: the requirements.txt of ansible, commitizen, copier, lizard and yamllint, and the
package-lock.json of codeceptjs and commitlint. The .config/megalinter folder ships only a package.json, which OSV does
OSV answers "No issues found", the summary marks osv-scanner green, and GitLab marks the job Passed. Package counts show
as <count>: they change with every dependency update.
